section_path: What's new in Django 5.0 > Minor features > Models
raw_text:
* The new ``violation_error_code`` attribute of
  :class:`~django.db.models.BaseConstraint`,
  :class:`~django.db.models.CheckConstraint`, and

raw_text:

section_path: Features deprecated in 4.2 > Miscellaneous
raw_text:
* The ``BaseUserManager.make_random_password()`` method is deprecated. See
  `recipes and best practices
  <https://docs.python.org/3/library/secrets.html#recipes-and-best-practices>`_

section_path: Backwards incompatible changes in 5.0 > Miscellaneous
raw_text:
* On databases without native support for the SQL ``XOR`` operator, ``^`` as
  the exclusive or (``XOR``) operator now returns rows that are matched by an
  odd number of operands rather than exactly one operand. This is consistent
  with the behavior of MySQL, MariaDB, and Python.
text: On databases without native support for the SQL XOR operator, ^ as the exclusive or (XOR) operator now returns rows that are matched by an odd number of operands rather than exactly one operand. This is consistent with the behavior of MySQL, MariaDB, and Python.

section_path: What's new in Django 5.1 > Minor features > Database backends
raw_text:
* ``"transaction_mode"`` option is now supported in :setting:`OPTIONS` on
  SQLite to allow specifying the :ref:`sqlite-transaction-behavior`.
text: "transaction_mode" option is now supported in OPTIONS on SQLite to allow specifying the sqlite-transaction-behavior.

section_path: What's new in Django 5.2 > Minor features > :mod:`django.contrib.auth`
raw_text:
* Auth backends can now provide async implementations which are used when
  calling async auth functions (e.g.
  :func:`~.django.contrib.auth.aauthenticate`) to reduce context-switching
  which improves performance. See :ref:`adding an async interface
  <writing-authentication-backends-async-interface>` for more details.
text: Auth backends can now provide async implementations which are used when calling async auth functions (e.g. django.contrib.auth.aauthenticate) to reduce context-switching which improves performance. See adding an async interface for more details.

section_path: What's new in Django 6.0 > Minor features > Email
raw_text:
* The new ``policy`` argument for :meth:`EmailMessage.message()
  <django.core.mail.EmailMessage.message>` allows specifying the email policy,
  the set of rules for updating and serializing the representation of the
  message. Defaults to :data:`email.policy.default`.
text: The new policy argument for EmailMessage.message() allows specifying the email policy, the set of rules for updating and serializing the representation of the message. Defaults to email.policy.default.

section_path: What's new in Django 4.2 > Minor features > Tests
raw_text:
* The :class:`~django.test.RequestFactory`,
  :class:`~django.test.AsyncRequestFactory`, :class:`~django.test.Client`, and

section_path: Features deprecated in 5.0 > Miscellaneous
raw_text:
* ``DatabaseOperations.field_cast_sql()`` is deprecated in favor of
  ``DatabaseOperations.lookup_cast()``. Starting with Django 6.0,
  ``BuiltinLookup.process_lhs()`` will no longer call ``field_cast_sql()``.
  Third-party database backends should implement ``lookup_cast()`` instead.
text: DatabaseOperations.field_cast_sql() is deprecated in favor of DatabaseOperations.lookup_cast(). Starting with Django 6.0, BuiltinLookup.process_lhs() will no longer call field_cast_sql(). Third-party database backends should implement lookup_cast() instead.

raw_text:

section_path: Backwards incompatible changes in 4.2 > Database backend API
raw_text:
* ``DatabaseFeatures.allows_group_by_pk`` is removed as it only remained to
  accommodate a MySQL extension that has been supplanted by proper functional
  dependency detection in MySQL 5.7.15. Note that
  ``DatabaseFeatures.allows_group_by_selected_pks`` is still supported and
  should be enabled if your backend supports functional dependency detection in
  ``GROUP BY`` clauses as specified by the ``SQL:1999`` standard.
text: DatabaseFeatures.allows_group_by_pk is removed as it only remained to accommodate a MySQL extension that has been supplanted by proper functional dependency detection in MySQL 5.7.15. Note that DatabaseFeatures.allows_group_by_selected_pks is still supported and should be enabled if your backend supports functional dependency detection in GROUP BY clauses as specified by the SQL:1999 standard.

section_path: Backwards incompatible changes in 5.1 > :mod:`django.contrib.gis`
raw_text:
* :class:`~django.contrib.gis.geoip2.GeoIP2` no longer opens both city and
  country databases when a directory path is provided, preferring the city
  database, if it is available. The country database is a subset of the city
  database and both are not typically needed. If you require use of the country
  database when in the same directory as the city database, explicitly pass the
  country database path to the constructor.
text: django.contrib.gis.geoip2.GeoIP2 no longer opens both city and country databases when a directory path is provided, preferring the city database, if it is available.
